items.name: Norte Chico Civilization
items.why: The oldest known urban civilization in the Americas (Caral, Peru), contemporary with the Old Kingdom. Dates are radiocarbon, c. 3000–1800 BCE. Fills the empty 2500–2001 BCE bin.

items.name: Caral Becomes a Monumental City
items.why: Platform mounds and sunken plazas at Caral, built while the pyramids rose in Egypt: a strong 'meanwhile' pairing. Radiocarbon range c. 2600–2000 BCE.

items.name: Chavín Culture
items.why: The first culture to spread one art style and religion across much of the Andes. Dates c. 900–200 BCE are approximate.

items.name: Teotihuacan
items.why: The largest city of the early Americas, perhaps 100,000 people. Rise c. 100 BCE, decline and burning c. 550 CE (dates debated by decades).

items.name: Teotihuacan's Pyramid of the Sun Built
items.why: One of the largest pyramids in the world. Main construction c. 200 CE (range c. 100–250).

items.name: Siyaj K'ak' Arrives at Tikal
items.why: Maya inscriptions record the arrival of a Teotihuacan-linked warlord in January 378 and a new Tikal dynasty the next year: an exactly dated contact between two great Mesoamerican cities.

items.name: Pakal the Great Becomes Ruler of Palenque
items.why: The best-known Maya king; his accession date (615) and his famous tomb are recorded in inscriptions. Gives Classic Maya a named person.

items.name: Moche Culture
items.why: North-coast Peru: irrigation, adobe pyramids and portrait pottery; the Lord of Sipán tomb. Dates c. 100–800 CE are approximate. Fills South America 1–999.

items.name: Chaco Canyon Culture
items.why: Ancestral Puebloan great houses and road network in New Mexico. Tree-ring dates make the building phases unusually precise, c. 850–1150.

items.name: Cahokia Grows into a City
items.why: The largest city north of Mexico before 1492, with Monks Mound. Its rapid growth ('big bang') is dated c. 1050.

items.name: Tenochtitlan Founded
items.why: The Aztec capital on Lake Texcoco. 1325 is the traditional date (some sources give 1345). Gives the Aztec Empire a founding.

items.name: Pachacuti Begins the Inca Expansion
items.why: The ruler who turned Cusco into an empire; would begin the Inca Empire span. 1438 is the traditional chronology; radiocarbon suggests the expansion began earlier.

items.name: Machu Picchu Built
items.why: The Inca royal estate, traditionally c. 1450 for Pachacuti; radiocarbon (2021) shows it was in use by c. 1420. Range c. 1420–1450.

items.name: Hatshepsut Becomes Pharaoh
items.why: One of the few women to rule Egypt as pharaoh. Regent from c. 1479 BCE, crowned a few years later. Fills the thin 1500–1001 BCE bins.

items.name: Akhenaten Introduces the Worship of the Aten
items.why: A pharaoh who made one god, the sun disc, the centre of state religion. Reign c. 1353–1336 BCE.

items.name: Battle of Kadesh
items.why: Egypt (Ramesses II) against the Hittites in Syria: the best-documented battle of the ancient world, followed by one of the earliest known peace treaties (c. 1259). Usually dated 1274 BCE.

items.name: Carthage Founded
items.why: The Phoenician colony that became Rome's great rival. 814 BCE is the traditional date; the earliest archaeology is late 9th century BCE.

items.name: Kushite King Piye Conquers Egypt
items.why: Kush, from today's Sudan, ruled Egypt as its 25th Dynasty: an African kingdom beyond Egypt in the timeline. Invasion c. 728 BCE.

items.name: Nok Culture
items.why: Central Nigeria: famous terracotta sculptures and some of the earliest iron smelting south of the Sahara. Recent research dates it c. 1500 BCE to the turn of the era; the sculptures c. 900 BCE onward.

items.name: Bantu Expansion
items.why: The spread of Bantu-speaking farmers and ironworkers across central, eastern and southern Africa. A gradual process, roughly 1000 BCE to 500 CE; the years are only a frame.

items.name: Library of Alexandria Founded
items.why: The great library of the ancient world, founded under Ptolemy I or II, c. 285 BCE (exact year unknown).

items.name: Arabs Conquer Egypt
items.why: Brings Egypt into the Islamic world and fills Africa's empty 500–999 bin. Invasion 639; Alexandria surrendered in 641 and was handed over in 642.

items.name: Lalibela's Rock-Hewn Churches Carved
items.why: Eleven churches cut from solid rock in Ethiopia under King Lalibela (reign c. 1181–1221). Year approximate.

items.name: Sundiata Keita Wins the Battle of Kirina
items.why: The founding victory of the Mali Empire; would begin the Mali span. Known from oral tradition (the Epic of Sundiata); c. 1235.

items.name: Ibn Battuta Visits the Mali Empire
items.why: The traveller's eyewitness account (1352–53) is a key written source for Mali at its height.

items.name: Swahili Coast Trading Cities
items.why: Kilwa, Mombasa, Zanzibar and others linked Africa to the Indian Ocean trade (gold from Great Zimbabwe passed through Kilwa). Their peak was roughly 1000–1500; Portuguese attacks began in 1505.

items.name: Trung Sisters Lead a Revolt Against Han Rule
items.why: Vietnam's national heroines drove out the Han governor in 40 CE and ruled until 43. Fills Southeast Asia before 1000.

items.name: Funan
items.why: The earliest known state in mainland Southeast Asia (Mekong delta), known from Chinese records and the port of Oc Eo. Dates c. 50–550 CE are approximate.

items.name: Earliest Srivijaya Inscription Carved
items.why: The Kedukan Bukit inscription (682) is the first record of Srivijaya, the Sumatran sea power. Would begin the Srivijaya span.

items.name: Borobudur Completed
items.why: The largest Buddhist monument in the world, in Java; built c. 780–830 under the Sailendra dynasty.

items.name: Battle of Bach Dang Ends Chinese Rule in Vietnam
items.why: Ngo Quyen's victory (938) ended about a thousand years of Chinese rule over northern Vietnam.

items.name: Anawrahta Founds the Pagan Empire
items.why: First unification of the Irrawaddy valley (Myanmar); Pagan's thousands of temples. 1044 is the traditional date of his accession.

items.name: Majapahit Founded
items.why: The Javanese empire founded in 1293, in the aftermath of the failed Mongol invasion of Java.

items.name: Kingdom of Ayutthaya Founded
items.why: The Siamese kingdom that later sacked Angkor (already in the db). 1351 is the traditional, widely used date.

items.name: Malacca Sultanate Founded
items.why: The port that controlled the Strait of Malacca until the Portuguese took it in 1511. Founded c. 1400 (traditions differ by a few years).

items.name: Lapita Voyagers Settle Remote Oceania
items.why: The first people to cross open ocean beyond sight of land, reaching Vanuatu, Fiji, Tonga and Samoa. Radiocarbon range c. 1100–800 BCE. Oceania has nothing before 1500 now.

items.name: Polynesians Settle Hawaii
items.why: Dates are debated: recent radiocarbon work favours c. 1000–1250; older estimates went as early as 300–800. Would be shown with that range.

items.name: Nan Madol Built on Pohnpei
items.why: A city of basalt islets in Micronesia, seat of the Saudeleur dynasty. Megalithic building began c. 1180–1200.

items.name: Polynesians Reach Rapa Nui
items.why: Easter Island, the far corner of the Polynesian triangle, settled c. 1150–1250; the moai followed.

items.name: Polynesian Voyagers Settle New Zealand
items.why: The last major landmass settled by humans; the ancestors of the Maori arrived c. 1250–1300 (a firm consensus).

items.name: Stonehenge's Sarsen Circle Raised
items.why: The great stones went up c. 2500 BCE (range c. 2600–2400); the site is older. Fills 2500–2001 BCE.

items.name: Ur-Nammu Issues the Earliest Surviving Law Code
items.why: About three centuries before Hammurabi's code (already in the db). Reign c. 2112–2095 BCE in the middle chronology.

items.name: Palace of Knossos Built
items.why: Centre of Minoan Crete, Europe's first palace civilization. First palace c. 1900 BCE (approximate).

items.name: Rigveda Composed
items.why: The oldest Hindu scripture, passed down orally for centuries; composed c. 1500–1200 BCE. South Asia has nothing between 2600 and 1000 BCE.

items.name: Oracle-Bone Writing Appears in Shang China
items.why: The earliest Chinese writing, from the reign of Wu Ding (c. 1250–1192 BCE). Gives the Shang span its signature event.

items.name: Late Bronze Age Collapse
items.why: Within a few decades the Hittite Empire, Mycenaean Greece and Ugarit fell and Egypt shrank. Causes are debated (drought, Sea Peoples, systems collapse). C. 1200–1150 BCE.

items.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
items.why: The first empire to rule from Egypt to Iran; Nineveh, Ashurbanipal's library. 911 (Adad-nirari II) to 609 BCE (the fall of Harran) are the conventional dates.

items.name: Buddhism Reaches Han China
items.why: By the 1st century CE Buddhism was in China; tradition ties it to Emperor Ming's dream and the White Horse Temple (c. 65–68).

items.name: Three Kingdoms of China
items.why: Wei, Shu and Wu after the fall of the Han; the setting of the Romance of the Three Kingdoms. Ends with the Jin reunification (already in the db).

items.name: Queen Himiko Sends an Envoy to Wei China
items.why: The first Japanese ruler known by name, recorded in Chinese chronicles in 239. Japan has nothing before 500 now.

items.name: Kofun Period
items.why: Japan's era of giant keyhole-shaped burial mounds and the rise of the Yamato state. Conventional dates c. 250–538.
